survivors.claim: D7/Contracts now promise 'aloneMs > budget is compared before any rounding', but the comparison still runs on a rounded integer: the confirming child prints Math.round(ms) on the MEASURED line and the parent parses that line with (\d+)ms, so the parent's entry.ms is the child's already-rounded value. The rounding moved from the parent to the child; it did not leave the comparison. A file whose true serial duration is in (budget, budget + 0.5) still prints '<budget>ms' from the child, compares as not-over, and is cleared as CONTENTION.
survivors.impact: The spec claims the boundary comparison is rounding-free and it is not; a file over budget by less than half a millisecond can still be cleared, and the amendment text describes a fix that was not implemented.
survivors.evidence: Spec D7 row and Contracts both say the comparison does not round first. Code line 142 in confirming mode yields Math.round(ms) on the MEASURED line; line 99 parent parse /^__FILE_BUDGET_MEASURED__ (.+) (\d+)ms( timedout)?$/gm; line 168 entry.ms > budget. The wire format the Contracts block itself fixes makes a pre-rounding comparison impossible in the parent unless the child emits the unrounded number.

survivors.claim: AC-20260910-01-10 promises 'the measured duration SHALL be the file's real serial duration, not the budget', and D7 says 'an offender measures truthfully', but the AC's own literal fixture does not deliver that: a 30ms test under SPEC_TEST_FILE_BUDGET_MS=5 is measured in the child as 12ms with the ' timedout' suffix (child timeout = 2 x 5 = 10ms), and the RED line prints 12ms, not 30ms. The verdict is correct via the timed-out rule, but the number is neither the real duration nor the budget, and the AC-10 pin asserts only RED/exit 1/no CONTENTION, never the measured number, so the test names the AC without testing that clause.
survivors.impact: The acceptance criterion states a guarantee the code does not provide for its own example, and the test that cites it never checks it.
survivors.evidence: Executed, HEAD reporter, confirming mode at budget 5 with child timeout 10: __FILE_BUDGET_MEASURED__ tests/thirty.test.js 12ms timedout, exit=1. Same fixture at budget 500 (child timeout 1000): 33ms, truthful because 30 < 2 x 500. AC-10 pin body asserts status, RED and absence of CONTENTION only.

survivors.claim: The timed-out-confirms rule can produce a self-contradictory RED line for a suspect that is under budget alone: any test carrying an explicit per-test timeout below 2 x budget that times out inside the serial child sets the ' timedout' suffix, and the parent then prints __FILE_BUDGET_RED__ with ms smaller than budget, advising a split of a file that is not over budget. Not a false exit code — the timed-out test already fails the run — but a false diagnosis. Reachable in this repo: chrome-harness (timeout 20000), release-legs (30000), design-atlas-serve-port (6000) all sit below the live 90000ms child timeout.
survivors.impact: When a contended file also has a genuinely timing-out test, the guard tells the developer to split the file instead of pointing at the failing test.
survivors.evidence: Executed: fixture with test('explicit short timeout', { timeout: 20 }, () => new Promise(() => {})). Child at budget 500 (timeout 1000): __FILE_BUDGET_MEASURED__ explicit.test.js 21ms timedout; the event carries failureType testTimeoutFailure at nesting 0. Line 123 marks any nesting-0 testTimeoutFailure regardless of whose timeout fired.

A hung subtest arrives as nesting 1 cancelledByParent and is filtered; a plain failing test is testCodeFailure and is not marked. The one path to a timedout mark with ms < budget is an explicit per-test timeout, reported as the soft finding above.
